newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Jan-Aug soymeal imports 560,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Thai Jan-Aug soymeal imports 560,000 tonnes.

text.p: Thailand has imported about 560,000 tonnes of soymeal under a calendar 1996 low-tariff government program between January and August, a commerce ministry official said on Monday.
The total import quota for soymeal imports is 830,000 tonnes, leaving 270,000 tonnes that may be imported by the end of this year, she told Reuters.
In the market, traders said the latest buying they had heard of was some weeks ago when feedmillers ordered 50,000 tonnes of low quality soymeal from Brazil for August-September shipment.
The prices were said to be below US$300 per tonne c and f Bangkok.
A G. Premjee trader said he had heard of another new order of 20,000 tonnes of soymeal for October shipment, also from Brazil but this could not be confirmed by other traders.
However, the high prices of overseas soymeal and the lower domestic prices curbed imports, they said.
"Prices of imported soymeal have increased by US$30-40 in the past month. We don't expect buyers to enter the market again until the overseas prices ease," said a trader from Cargill Siam.
Currently 48 percent-protein soymeal from Brazil costs around US$335 per tonne c and f Bangkok.
This imported soymeal under the government's low-tariff program is subjected to 15 percent tariff plus other expenses.
Those who do not receive or have used up their quota will have to pay extra 500 baht (US$20) per tonne if they want to buy imported soymeal from quota holders.
These extra expenses make the cost of imported soymeal higher than locally crushed soymeal.
Soymeal from locally crushed imported soybeans sells at around 9,700 baht per tonne ex factory.
